data.title: SLC Agrícola Launches First R$515 Million Rural Notes Issuance for Agribusiness Funding
data.description:
SLC Agricola S.A. ( (BR:SLCE3) ) has provided an announcement.

SLC Agrícola S.A. has approved its first issuance of book-entry rural product notes with financial settlement, totaling R$515.48 million, in a single seven-year series aimed exclusively at professional investors. The notes will be publicly distributed under automatic registration, carry remuneration linked to 95.5% of the DI Rate with amortization in two equal installments, and are fully backed by a 100% bank guarantee from Banco Bradesco S.A.

The company will fully swap the proceeds into U.S. dollars, making the effective transaction reflect dollar variation plus a 6.15% annual spread, aligning its funding structure with its currency exposure. All funds will be directed to agribusiness-related activities within its corporate purpose, supporting production, commercialization, processing and associated operating costs and investments, which may strengthen its capital base and operational capacity in Brazil’s agricultural market.

data.title: Acadia Pharmaceuticals Reaches Preliminary Derivative Lawsuit Settlement
data.description:
ACADIA Pharmaceuticals ( (ACAD) ) has provided an announcement.

On August 24, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California preliminarily approved a settlement of a stockholder derivative action and related Section 220 books-and-records and litigation demands brought on behalf of Acadia Pharmaceuticals. The case, Kanner et al. v. Biggar et al., stems from allegations that certain officers and directors breached fiduciary duties and engaged in misconduct tied to regulatory setbacks for pimavanserin.

The derivative action followed Acadia’s March and April 2021 disclosures that the FDA had issued a deficiency letter and Complete Response Letter rejecting the company’s supplemental New Drug Application seeking to expand pimavanserin’s use to dementia-related psychosis, which triggered sharp share price declines. The settlement, which will be considered at a court hearing scheduled for January 13, 2027, runs alongside still-pending securities class and opt-out actions, signaling ongoing legal and governance scrutiny that could shape Acadia’s risk profile and stakeholder confidence.
